description.narrative:
Affordability/Environmental: The Project is expected to generate 56GWh/year of electricity and benefit ~16,000 people. The plant will partly replace a 13MW diesel gas turbine thus contributing to reduce the countrys reliance in fossil fuels (currently over 95%) and the resulting high exposure to fuel price volatility, which is directly reflected in the end consumers bills since it is passed down to via the FCA mechanism. The associated emissions savings per year are preliminarily estimated at 45,000 tCO2.
Sustainability: The Projects demonstration effect can be a central component of the country decarbonization strategy for the power sector. The Project directly supports Barbados's National Energy Policy, which targets 95% renewable energy and carbon-neutral island-state transformation by 2030. The Renewstable concept combining Photovoltaics (PV) and Hydrogen (H2) generation with H2 and Li-Ion storage represents a significant innovation to provide stable baseload and dispatchable energy to the grid, enabling increased utilization of solar generation in the countrys power generation matrix and thus mitigating climate change effects of the sector. Barbadoss generation matrix relies heavily in fossil fuel generated power and the role of solar power in the provision of electricity has remained marginal because of its limited ability to dispatch based on changes in demand, which the projects configuration contribute to address, thus effectively diversifying sources of generation, and reducing the reliance on thermal sources.

The proposed investment consists of a senior secured financing package of ~US$[130] million for the construction of a 50MWp solar plant with a 15MW (30WMh) lithium-ion battery (BESS) and 90MWh hydrogen storage capabilities in Barbados (the Project or RSB). The Project is expected to be supported by the Green Climate Fund as described in the Blended Finance Section. IFC is planning on bringing US$41 million in concessional blended finance funds (US$40million senior secured loan and US$1 million grant) from the Green Climate Fund (GCF board approval received in Oct-23). The concessional blended finance funds brought by IFC would be part of the debt package for which IFC is mobilizing a further US$70 million from local/regional banks jointly with IDB Invest.
